fields.meta_title: Service Landing Page: Build One Per Service | Emergent
fields.meta_description: A service landing page sells one job. See four examples, from a ZIP code check to a capped moving calendar, and build yours by prompt.
fields.h1: Build a Service Landing Page for Each Job You Sell
fields.hero_description: Build a service landing page that sells one job, checks the visitor's ZIP code, and saves each request to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Single-Service Page Needs to Book Jobs
fields.features_subheading: A service landing page sells one job to people who need it done. These six parts take a visitor from the offer to a booked request.
fields.feature_1:
A form shaped by the job

Ask only what this one service needs, such as the tank size for a water heater install. Emergent builds the form from your prompt, and you add or drop a field by prompting.
fields.feature_2:
A ZIP code check up front

List the ZIP codes your trucks reach, and the page checks each visitor's ZIP before the form opens. Anyone outside that list sees a short note in place of the booking form.
fields.feature_3:
Every request as a row you own

Each request lands in a database you own, with the service, the address, and the time it arrived. Sort the rows by ZIP code or by date, and export them whenever you like.
fields.feature_4:
An alert to whoever does the work

Name the person who handles each kind of request, and the app sends them an email or Slack alert when one arrives. A termite job reaches the inspector, not the front desk.
fields.feature_5:
A web address customers recognize

Publish the page on the domain already printed on your trucks and invoices, or on a subdomain of that domain. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.
fields.feature_6:
Free to start, with code to keep

The free tier covers building and publishing the page. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the page and its data on any server you choose.

fields.usecase_heading: Service Landing Page Examples by Trade
fields.tab_content_1:
84 requests sorted by ZIP into two lists

Pinecastle Plumbing installs water heaters, and this page sells only that job. The first field asks for a ZIP code. Of 84 requests last month, 69 came from ZIP codes the crew serves and went on to pick an install window. The other 15 saw an out-of-area note and were saved to a separate list.
fields.tab_content_2:
Cleaning 2 weeks apart won 33 of 60 signups

A cleaning customer buys a schedule, not a single visit. Graylock Cleaning's page prices each visit by how often it repeats: $120 weekly, $140 every 2 weeks, or $165 monthly. The button shows the price of the chosen plan. Of 60 signups this month, 18 chose weekly, 33 chose every 2 weeks, and 9 chose monthly.
fields.tab_content_3:
Termite requests go straight to Corin

Mosswick Pest Control asks one question first: which pest is the visitor seeing? A request that names termites emails Corin Lemoyne, the termite inspector, with the address in it. Every other pest goes to the scheduling desk. Of 22 requests this week, 7 named termites and 15 named another pest.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each Saturday closes after its 4th move

Halverson Movers takes 4 moves per Saturday, and the date picker shows how many spots each Saturday has left. Right now November 7 shows 2 of 4. When a date's 4th move is booked, that Saturday leaves the picker, and nobody can book a crew the company does not have.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Service Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a service landing page that sells one job, covers your service area, and turns visitors into booked requests.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one service this page sells
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Draw the service area as ZIP codes
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Print the price when the job has one
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single job, such as a water heater install or a weekly cleaning, and write the headline and the form around it. Someone who searched for drain cleaning should land on drain cleaning, not on a list of every service you offer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write down the ZIP codes your crews reach and name the area in plain words near the top. In the page markup, schema.org's areaServed property describes the geographic area where a service or offered item is provided.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Show a number when the job has one: a flat install fee, a price per visit, or a starting price with what raises it. Leave the price off when the cost depends on what the crew finds on site, and say that an estimate comes first.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Open the form with the question that decides who handles the request, such as the ZIP code or the pest, and save name and phone for the end. A visitor outside your area then finds out before typing a street address.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Make the phone number one tap
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put a call button near the top and repeat the number in the footer. Google's local business guidance asks for the country code and area code in the phone number, so write the number the same way on the page and in the markup.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Use photos of finished work from your own crews, with the town named in each caption. Pick reviews that mention the service the page sells. A water heater page should quote a customer who had a water heater installed.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and send a test request
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the service and who takes each request, and Emergent builds the page with a request table behind it. Open it on a phone, submit a test request, and check that the row lands and the alert reaches the right person.

faq_plan.q: What is a service landing page?
faq_plan.a: A service landing page is a single web page that sells one service, such as a furnace repair or a lawn mowing plan, and asks the visitor to request it. It carries the offer, the area served, the price or how pricing works, and one form or call button, with nothing that leads away from the request.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Pick the one service the page sells and list the ZIP codes you cover, then describe both to Emergent's AI landing page builder, along with who should hear about each request. Emergent builds the page and the database behind it from that prompt, and you change the offer or the form later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should a landing page for my service business ask visitors to do?
faq_plan.a: Ask for one thing: a request for the service the page sells, or a phone call. Match the action to how the job gets scheduled. A fixed-price visit can be booked straight from the form, while a job that needs an estimate should end in a request for one. Keep a second, competing button off the page.

faq_plan.q: What makes the best landing page for a service business?
faq_plan.ref: best landing page for service business
faq_plan.secondary: best landing page for service business
faq_plan.a: One job, one service area, and a plain next step make the best page: a price or an estimate, a short form, and a phone number. Write one page per service, not one for the whole company. A general business landing page suits offers that are not a single job, such as wholesale orders or catering.

faq_plan.q: What do the strongest landing page examples for services have in common?
faq_plan.a: Each of the four examples above sells one job and runs one rule behind its form: a ZIP code check, a price per visit, a route to the right person, or a cap on bookings per Saturday. When you study any service page, look for that rule first. It decides what happens after the visitor presses the button.

faq_plan.q: What should a tree service landing page include?
faq_plan.hint: Can you give me a tree service landing page template?
faq_plan.a: Include the jobs the crew does, such as removal, trimming, or stump grinding, as separate choices on the form, plus the ZIP codes you cover. Ask where the tree stands and whether it is near the house or power lines; the estimator needs both before the site visit. Photos of finished jobs from your own crew do more than stock images.

faq_plan.q: How do I write a service landing page that sells to other companies?
faq_plan.hint: How to sell web design services landing pages?
faq_plan.a: Name the business result in the headline, show the scope of the service and the kind of company it suits, and end with one request, such as a site visit or a call. Put the commercial details on the page too, like the hours your crews work and how you invoice. A b2b landing page covers longer buying decisions with several people involved.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a separate service landing page for each service I offer?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when you send ads or mailers to that service. A visitor who searched for gutter cleaning should see gutter cleaning first. Keep a combined services page on your main site for browsing. Emergent builds each page from its own prompt, and every page's requests land in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I track which ads bring requests to my service business landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give each ad its own link with a campaign tag, and add a hidden field to the form that saves that tag with the request. Count requests by tag each week and cut the ads that send none. Requests from a page Emergent builds are stored in a database you own, and each row carries the tag beside the request details.

faq_plan.q: How do I send people from a printed flyer to my service landing page?
faq_plan.a: Print a QR code and a short web address that open the page for the one service on the flyer, not your home page. A qr code landing page is read on a phone. Keep its first screen light: web.dev says sites should strive to have Largest Contentful Paint of 2.5 seconds or less. Repeat the offer from the print at the top.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3); the AlsoAsked tree asks for an example of a service page and how to create one, and template galleries answer with a pretty page that stops at the button. This page wins by showing four service landing pages built around one service each (a water heater install, a recurring home cleaning, a pest inspection, a Saturday move) and the mechanism each service needs: a ZIP check against the service area, a price per visit by frequency, routing by the problem the visitor names, and a cap on jobs per day. The business landing page sibling owns goal-based pages (quote, wholesale, consultation, catering); this page owns the single-service page and stays off those goals. B2B, local business and pricing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: "Pinecastle Plumbing installs water heaters, and this page sells only that job.", "A cleaning customer buys a schedule, not a single visit.", "Mosswick Pest Control asks one question first".

craft.evidence: One ", so" ending (step 5), under the cap; sentences vary ("Keep a second, competing button off the page."). Q9 repetition of "request" kept as a note.

voice.evidence: Plain operator voice, concrete details: "Of 84 requests last month, 69 came from ZIP codes the crew serves", "nobody can book a crew the company does not have". No AI tells found.

truth.evidence: claims_used prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, custom-domain, code-export, free-start all in rules/capabilities.json; step 2 matches schema.org quote "The geographic area where a service or offered item is provided."; step 5 matches Google quote on country and area code; FAQ 10 quotes web.dev LCP 2.5 s verbatim; table cells are single-vendor library entries (Unbounce, Landingi, Wix); numbers add up (69+15=84, 18+33+9=60, 7+15=22, 2 of 4); November 7, 2026 is a Saturday.
